When it comes to Jackbox Party Packs, this is my favorite so far -- maybe the only one in which I actually like all the games.

I love the Drawful games, and to animate things makes it even more hilarious than it used to be. There is also a fantastic Friend Mode.
The cool thing about The Wheel is that you do not answer regular questions. You tap all the right answers, or you have to type out a word. The fun part too is that there is an element of luck, which keeps the game interesting for all players.
The word game of the pack Job Job might be the weakest one. You create new sentences with words from other players, which is a hit or miss. The setting of a boring office seems to be somehow off-putting as well. Still fun though.
The Poll Mine is the game everyone wants to keep playing. It is like Family Feud, but your group answered the questions. Technically, you can play it with two people, but it does not really make sense. I would say four is the minimum.
And Weapons Drawn. A hybrid between writing, drawing and guessing. Amazing. First, you have to come up with a name for a character, but people will guess if you typed in the name, so it cannot be something obvious. Then you have to hide a letter in a drawing. Then you have to find out who the other drawings belong to,  basically. It is a really cool game.

Keep in mind that you play with one smartphone / tablet or web browser per person. If you want to play with your friends online, you can use Steam Remote Play or Discord. It is still fun.

The games were all pretty fun although the trivia one (The Wheel) was kinda meh. Job Job is absolutely the best with Weapons Drawn and Poll Mine tied for second (albeit requiring more energy/thought). Def a fun pack
Pretty fun to play with a big group of friends, but you probably will play this game more in moderation.

Overall concensus: Probably one of the better packs. Cap was raised to 10 players, 2 of the games are BANGERS, 2 are playable, only 1 is completely godawful

Drawful Animate: Pass, just play another Drawful if you have it. Rarely, if ever, does a 2 frame animation allow more expression than just a single image. Call us a bunch of uncreative idiots, but no one ever did anything animated and just redrew the first frame again, making it double the effort (and time) for every round with no payoff. And Drawful still has really basic drawing controls compared to other drawing games from previous packs like Champ'd Up and TKO.

Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Pass. Slightly more trivia and significantly less getting uncontrollably screwed over compared to Murder Trivia Party, but that's not saying much. Yet I would still rather play Trivia Murder Party, because the trivia in Wheel is mostly selecting the answers from lists ("select every member of Monty Python" or "every form of poetry"), and lists are pretty lame because barely will you know every answer and are barely penalized for getting wrong answers. Plus the minigames in Murder Party are a lot more engaging, quick, and have a chance for frantic collaborating with your group, while Wheel is just... spinning a completely random wheel with no input from the audience, so sometimes Wheel can feel *more* random and inconsequential than Murder Party.

Weapons Drawn: PASS. For one, it's just so LONG, I think the only game we played took a half hour, while most other games in this pack don't pass the ten minute mark per game. Well, it felt like a half hour to us. So it's an extra long commitment, and... well, the concept isn't bad, but it's just so easy to cheese. People can choose to ignore the drawing prompt and hide their clue in a sea of scribbles, and there's no actual way to punish them, and in fact they get rewarded for this because you can't deduce who made the drawing. And even if you have a group of friends who decide to follow the prompts and not be shitheads, the point system is really scattered, and nobody was ever certain they were winning or in dead last until the very end of the game. It's a social deduction game where it's too easy to not follow the rules and win, and a win felt random and undeserved. Also the drawing system is still extremely limited, and the magnifying glass during the investigation phase controls like the X button in a popup advertisement. Horrendous.

Job Job: A must have. Every game has been a riot, and the prompts are all solid with no "how the hell am I supposed to answer this?" questions like in Quiplash. Probably a top 5 Jackbox game for everyone I've played it with, maybe even our #1.

Poll Mine: Ranges from the most fun you'll have, to mid at best. Some polls I swear we were seconds away from drawing blood and spent the entire debate time shouting, because a team member chaotically admits to putting a stupid answer as the #1 on their poll, completely throwing out the presumed ranking and potentially spiraling your team out of control. A fantastic time. Other times the prompt is just so awful you are unenthusiastically forced to guess your way out, which leads to a lot of wrong answers and a lot of "sure, I don't really care, we all just put random stuff down so who would have guessed?" from the whole group. And I swear, every time I have introduced a new person to this game, one of the prompts is something like "Rank all players in this current game on who is most likely to ______" which is just awkward because they're excluded from inside jokes and never picked. The bad games are bad, but the good games are SO GOOD. If this game had a way to select what prompts are played each round, this game would be #1 GOAT Jackbox game. And having players voting for the top option isn't even a wild suggestion, THE WHOLE GAME IS ABOUT CHOOSING YOUR TOP OPTION FROM A LIST.

I will start with my general opinion of the pack and then do a short review of each game within the pack.

This is probably one of the best JPP games if not the best so far. My friends and I are still a bit unsure about "Weapons Drawn", but all the others are really enjoyable. And even "Weapons Drawn" still has a good idea behind it, it's just a lot more convoluted for newer players, so we'll be giving it a bit more of a shot in the future but even the only game we don't love, we can still see that it has potential.

[b][u]Drawful Animate :[/u][/b] If you've played Drawful before, you probably have a good idea what to expect here. You basically draw the basic drawing and follow it with a separate frame. I think it could benefit from other gamemodes, perhaps things like "3 frames" gamemodes and whatnot. But it's good fun.

[b][u]Job Job :[/u][/b] This is a pretty weird one. You have to answer very random questions, then use the words everyone in the group have used for those answers to make up your answer for the next questions, it can make for some pretty funny answers.

[b][u]Poll Mine :[/u][/b] This is really just a trivia game but in teams. It can be pretty chaotic when people are opinionated but that's what makes it funny. I wouldn't suggest this one unless you have at least 6 players, though. It's surprisingly entertaining, though.

[b][u]Weapons Drawn :[/u][/b] As I stated previously; this game is quite convoluted and takes a lot of learning to understand it. But it definitely has potential, and it has multiple steps that can be pretty funny. But it feels a bit weird and will often end up with people trying to speak over each other to make their points/trying to fool others. It's a bit messier than the other games in the pack but I could definitely see this going somewhere in the future.

[b][u]The Wheel of Enormous Proportions :[/u][/b] This was probably the biggest surprise. Pretty much none of us in my friend group are into gambling/RNG. So going into a "Spin the Wheel" type of game, we didn't expect too much. But this is essentially just a big trivia game with some pretty chaotic aspects. I think this turned out to be the best-made one in the pack.

[b][u]TL;DR[/u][/b] : Each game is at the very least "Decent". If you like JPP games normally, it shouldn't be any different this time around.

GAMES RANKED BEST TO WORST
*Job Job: The 'write funny stuff' and make your friends laugh game of this game. This is the best one. Like all joke games, this will be benefited by a funnier friend group, although I think the fridge magnet mechanic of picking words makes it easier to think of funny things than some of the other games. We laughed really, really hard at this one though and it's novel.

*The Poll Mine: Family feud style game with also some team vs team 'Codenames' type mechanics. Simple enough concept but opens itself up to surprising depth of strategy and interesting discussions. We replayed this one a couple times as well because we loved it.

*Drawful Animate: Like the title says, this is your classic Drawful with a fun but not super game-changing twist. The animation aspect is pretty intuitive, you now do two panels. If your group likes Drawful this is absolutely worth playing, it's solid.

*Weapons Drawn: I think with a few more grounds this might edge above Drawful, though there's a lot to learn the first time playing this and I think it could have been slightly more streamlined. It's kind of a mafia/werewolf type (social deduction) game with drawings. The core conceit of hiding letters in drawings is good, though and leads to some interesting results.

*The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: Easily the weakest game by a mile. It's essentially a plain trivia game with a drawn out randomised wheel mechanic. I appreciate mixing up the theme from Trivia Murder Party with something more upbeat, but there's nothing really special about this one. It's still 'fine enough' but I don't think most players would be drawn to play this like some of the others.

Overall, despite the Wheel being a bit weaker than the other games, all the others are extremely good and this is a very fine offering from Jackbox.

[i] The party game staple Jackbox returns with its eighth release. Does it have what it takes to keep the legacy going strong? [/i]

[b] Overview [/b]
Party games require two key elements to live up to the expectations of the genre. First, they have to be easily accessible as the minimum number of players to get the game functioning is higher than in most genres. Second, they have to be easy to pick up so that players can hop in and get right to the fun with the least amount of initial investment possible. Jackbox tends to succeed in this regard with most of the games in its collection even if they are a mixed bag at times. The eighth entry in the series carries on the trend with a handful of games that are likely to entertain and disappoint in equal measure. I was lucky enough to have several good friends along for the ride and I’ve decided to rank the contents of this pack from the least impressive to most impressive experiences on offer.


[b] #5: The Wheel of Enormous Proportions [/b]
The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is most easily defined as a combination of trivia and Wheel of Fortune. A multiple-choice question is posed to the group with well over a dozen answers. Many of these choices are correct and the player who selects the most correct and least incorrect among them is awarded the most points. The highest-scoring player receives a slice to put onto the wheel that is visited after every trio of questions. When the trivia action moves to the wheel, each player places their collected slices onto it and a lucky player gives it a spin. Whoever’s space it lands on receives a hefty batch of points with a few surprise landings on it to spice things up as well.

Every game is going to be subjectively judged and opinions may vary, though this was the game that the group unanimously decided was the worst in the pack. Trivia is hit-or-miss for me in general and I tend to get bored of it quickly, though it was a perfect storm of issues that lost me on this one. A short time restricted the amount of time that choices could be made and left a couple of the players who were playing on their phones frustrated as those using a browser had a serious advantage. I can certainly get on board with timed trivia, but time trivia that requires you to scroll on a smartphone while simply being point and click in a browser was rough. The wheel itself, the real gimmick of Wheel of Enormous Proportions, didn’t add much to the excitement either and there was a collective groan at one point when a near-win resulted in an entire additional round thrown on. This one’s likely to be a hard pass for me in the future unless someone else gets an urge to play and asks me to join in.


[b] #4: Weapons Drawn [/b]
Weapons Drawn is a unique enough game, though where it bogs down is its complexity. Jackbox tends to pull in groups of players who are seeking out something quick, comedic, and casual to play with their friends but this one doesn’t fit as closely as the others as it has an initial learning curve that ends up slowing down the play session for an experience that, quite bluntly put, isn’t worth it even once everyone has it down. Each player is both a murderer and a detective who is tasked with drawing a murder weapon from a prompt. The catch is that a letter from your name is used as your calling card, something that links a murder to you, and you have to hide it as well as you can inside of your drawing. Depending on the letter this can be a particularly arduous task or extremely easy (I’m looking at you ‘I’). Players will then name their own guest they’re bringing to the party and the group will have to figure out who killed each others’ guests by judging the pictures that show up.

Although I wouldn’t say that Weapons Drawn was a bad experience, it wasn’t a thrilling one. It was less casual than the others in the pack and even after the investment required to learn it was behind us, we felt that we were mostly done with it before we’d even reached the end of our first run. If a murder mystery party game is what you’re looking for, I would highly suggest looking elsewhere at plenty of other places that do it better.


[b] #3: The Poll Mine [/b]
Although my opinions have been a bit harsh, The Poll Mine comes in at number three and acts as the turning point. Each player is assigned to one of two teams that were named by the players themselves and takes off on an adventure where each location tasks them with answering a question in the form of a ranked poll. Teams then guess where the different answers ended up in the ranking in order to acquire the most torches with correct answers.

This one was a hit with most of the group and I could definitely see jumping back into it in the future. It’s a good time guessing how your friends voted in the ranking and the variety of questions keeps it fresh. There’s a strong interpersonal element that wasn’t in the previous two entries that made this one stand out as a fun experience that has you continually guessing how the rest of the players lined up their choices in a particularly subjective poll.


[b] #2: Drawful Animate [/b]
The silver trophy goes to Drawful Animate. In this one, players receive a secret text prompt and have to draw it before the game begins. However, these pieces of art have a unique twist to them in that you’re drawing two frames that become an animation to be viewed by the group. These are revealed one at a time and the non-artist players submit their own fake prompts in an attempt to trick the others into voting for theirs instead of the right one. Points are awarded both for guessing the correct prompt and for having others vote for the false one that was added to the mix.

This was the game that felt the most like what I expected from Jackbox. It was fun and full of hilarious results hand-crafted by the personalities within the group. There was plenty of room for individuality and it was used to its full potential. I’m already getting the urge to play this one again and I would say that most of the conversations that have taken place since we ran through this pack have revolved around Drawful Animate.


[b] #1: Job Job [/b]
The standout game this time around is the job interview “simulation” Job Job. Players compete as candidates for a position by answering a variety of icebreaker questions in their own words. Once these answers are submitted, they’re chopped up into their individual words and thrown together into one large batch. They are then distributed amongst the players so that they may answer new questions using only these words. They can be placed in any order, though players no longer have the ability to type in their own at this point. Points are awarded both by having your own words picked to create the new answers or by having your Frankstein-monster of a sentence voted as a better fit than the other player’s that it’s lined up against.

Job Job was a pleasant surprise as it checked all of the boxes for what I wanted out of a Jackbox game while also being something new. Everyone got a kick out of the sentence restructuring and guessing which players certain words in the jumble had come from. It was a tough call between Drawful Animate and Job Job for the top spot, but Job Job pulled off the win due to its uniqueness.

[b] Verdict [/b]
The Jackbox Party Pack 8 lives up to its legacy with a few strong entries that are great additions to the collection overall. It’s likely to offer hours of fun for just about any group of players who are looking for a hilarious, personalized party game experience. That said, I would recommend waiting for a sale as it’s not the cheapest party game out there and there’s at least one entry that gets old before you’ve even finished your first game of it.

The newest Jackbox Party Pack is bound to bring a fun time to any gathering. If you've played any games from any of the other party packs, then you'll know that your phone/pc is the controller, and that only the host needs the game. The games in this pack range from okay to really good. But what games end up as the fan favorite of your gathering depends on who you're playing with. However, there have been two quality of life changes that are worth noting in my opinion.
1. Pressing escape brings up a menu that allows you to exit back to the game, to the pack's main menu, and to exit to desktop.
2. The games "Drawful: Animate" "Job Job" and "Weapons Drawn" have an option to disable timers. At the time of writing, I haven't been able to test this, but for those who don't want timers on these games, it is a nice option.

Now with the quality of life changes noted, I think it's time to look at the games in the pack.

1. DRAWFUL: ANIMATE
Easily the weakest game of the pack, in my opinion. The two-frame animations add alot to the Drawful experience, easily making Drawful: Animate the definitive Drawful experience, but the lack of an undo button or eraser in drawing makes Drawful Animate a game I'm less likely to pick over games like Gartic Phone or Skribblio. Despite this, Drawful: Animate can easily bring the laughs and is a good supporting addition to the pack.

2. THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS
This is the pack's trivia game. However, the Wheel of Enormous Proportions (which I'm gonna call "the Wheel" from now on) takes the trivia game and makes it radically different from the other trivia games in the other packs. Instead of choosing between three or four choices in games like Fibbage or Trivia Murder Party, most questions will have at least ten possible answers that you're probably not gonna get completely correct. Some questions will require you to match pairs, and some questions will need you to guess what the wheel is thinking of. In all other Jackbox trivia games, answering correctly will net you points, but in the Wheel, you also need luck to win the game. First to 20,000 points and land on a winning spot  on the winner's wheel will net you the win. The Wheel gives a good time for all, especially since the large amount of potential answers means that everyone will likely have to guess each question, meaning that nearly anyone could get a slice on the wheel.

3. JOB JOB
Easily my personal favorite game from the pack. The premise of Job Job is simple: You're answering common job interview questions by using some of the words said by the other players, which can lead to cursed quotes depending on what everyone else said. Job Job without context sounds incredibly boring (I mean who wants to answer job interview questions for fun?) but one of the Jackbox Party Packs' specialties, in my opinion is making games with boring premises into chaotic messes with good execution. Also this game uses Microsoft Office's Word Art. Need I say anything else?

4. POLL MINE
Poll Mine tasks tasks two teams of players with escaping a cave or dungeon by making both teams do three poll-related challenges where everyone needs to answer a poll and then both teams try to figure out what options were chosen in a few specific positions by everyone in order to gain or lose torches. The first two challenges have no real consequences if you lose all of your torches, but if one team loses all torches in the last challenge and the other team gets the next poll position right, the team that answered that question right wins. Poll Mine is a fun game that encourages you to know everyone in the room better than everyone knows you in order to win.

5. WEAPONS DRAWN
Weapons Drawn feels similar to Among Us but if everyone was both an Impostor and a Crewmate at the same time. In Weapons Drawn, you hide one of your in-game name's' letters in a drawing of a random item the game gives you (like a can opener or a book). You use your drawn weapons to murder one of two "guests" that another player named.  Then the game becomes a typical Among Us emergency meeting after the murders happen while the murderer is decided. Weapons Drawn is a more interesting take on the Social Deduction game due to everyone being both a murderer and detective and can lead to some intense arguments seen in many Among Us games, just don't put extended timers on if you don't want the game to take forever.

Overall, the most recent Jackbox Party Pack is a hit like always and is bound to make any gathering more fun.

As someone who has enjoyed all packs, especially pack 7, I was looking forward to see if this game would deliver to the same heights as the previous packs. I'll be going over the games in a (somewhat) simplistic manor, as who cares for reading anyway.

[Games were played in a discord server with below max players. That does heavily change things at least in my opinion.]

Drawful Animate: The original drawful is good, and this one is too. The only real difference between this and regular drawful is the fact you can animate your drawings. Something that kind of upset those I played with was the fact that the baseline prompts given were a tad too specific. If you wanted to do the even slightest of joke prompt, it stuck out like a sore thumb. Still a decent game, just need to adapt to the prompts.

Wheel of Enormous Proportions: I really like trivia games for some reason, even if I absolutely suck at trivia. Something that was neat about this game was the fact that it seemed like it was a child of You Don't Know Jack and Trivia Murder Party. A ton of shared aspects combined that made this game uniquely fun. Would've liked to have maybe played more than one time, but the rest of those playing did not seem to enjoy the game as much as I did.

Job Job: Voted probably best game out of the pack between me and those I played with. You fill out the prompts the game gives you and then afterwords you must use words from other players' responses to create the ultimate funnypost response to another prompt. Profanity filter needs to be turned off for maximum enjoyment. 

Poll Mine: Again, another game that probably needs maximum players as possible for most fun. The players are split into two teams to try to further the amount of torches (points) each team gets. Answering random polls, people will need to vote on the most voted answers for torches, and eventually vice versa. Does this for a round or two and that pretty much wraps up the game. Game isn't the greatest but it isn't bad either.

Weapons Drawn: Those I played with felt mixed about the game including myself. The premise is easy once you complete a game, but for the first game it just seemed confusing on what you're supposed to do. Mixing a pre-generated letter from your name, you must combine it with a drawing of yours to avert suspicious from you throughout the game. You need to successfully murder to even be classified as a murderer (duh?), but once you do people need to make context clues from your drawings to see if they can put two and two together. It's the same premise for 2-3 rounds or so. Points in this game were won solely on the fact if A. you committed a murder, B. Solved a murder, or C. fooled players. Maybe once we revisit the game we'll enjoy it more, but for now it was just okay. 

Overall, the pack to me isn't as good as pack 7. I'll just say it now. In my honest opinion you do need maximum players for all games to really settle into it. There's still plenty of fun to be had either way with all of the games in their own way.

DRAWFUL ANIMATE:

 THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS:

So i Pre Purchased this pack expecting more Jackbox... well i mean that is what i got, but what I wasn't expecting was just the amount of quality these games all had. This has to be the most quality Party Pack out of the five that i played (The others being 4, 5, 6, and 7) Not a single game was really a meh for me. I can see myself coming back to all of these games.

[h1]Drawful Animate[/h1]

Drawful... only with ANIMATION! Yeah its that simple, its drawful but with 2 frame animations instead of flat pictures. You get a prompt and you have to make a small moving picture based on that prompt. Once everyone finishes drawing, then everyone else has to then make a fake prompt to try and fool the other players and then guess what the real prompt for the drawing was. Good stuff Yeah. It's simple, doesn't go on for too long, and the small animation you get really brings a nice spice up to a familiar game.

[h1]The Wheel of Enormous Proportions[/h1]

A trivia game with a healthy dose of mario party-esque randomness.  You answer questions to get wedges and after three rounds of questions you put them on the titular wheel and spin to get points. The catch is the real moneymaker, the wheel spinning, is completely random. You can be doing REALLY well in the question and have a bunch of wedges on the board but the wheel could potentially not land on them at all. It's complete random chance and chaos, making this a trivia game where you can suck at trivia but STILL come out on top if your luck is good enough. Really chaotic and I had a blast playing this with friends

[h1]Job Job[/h1]

The standout game for Party Pack 8 in my opinion anyway. This one had almost nonstop laughter between my friends while we were playing. You start each round by answering prompts with sentences (5 words or more), then those sentences get sent to other players where they have to answer questions using on the words said in those sentences. (Or just from the question and writing prompt haha) This game leads to some random a hell (and very likely nonsensical) responses from every player. I don't know what else to say about this one, it was just pure joy to play.

[h1]The Poll Mines[/h1] 

This game splits you into two teams and then for each round will give everyone a survey to answer honestly. Once everyone answers the game then will ask each team (one at a time) to pick a door each represented by a choice from the survey. The goal is to guess which choice came in a certain position depending on what the game asked of you (Example: 1st 2nd, 3rd or 2nd 3rd and 4th) Its a nice team effort that leads to some really intense moments as once you hit the final level your points (Tallied by torches) get taken away for every one you get wrong. The game is another standout of the pack and was a lot of fun to play. 

[h1]Weapons Drawn[/h1]

Okay this is the only one that didn't 100% jive with the rest of my team though I wouldn't say its a downright stinker or 'meh' game. You take the role of a murderer/detective and have to draw a murder weapon to murder someone with... the weapon must contain a pre-drawn letter from your own name as a calling card, so the catch is to incorporate the letter into the drawing discreetly. But you also have to guess who murdered someone else and try to figure out THEIR calling card, making this a game of trying to figure out symbols and who drew what. It takes a bit and the rules for winning weren't 100% concise if im honest. But I still had fun trying to figure out who dun-it being a fan of games like Ace Attorney and such.

------------

So overall just about all of these games were fun to play, and I can see myself replaying all of these at some point... at least compared to most of the other party packs. I'd recommend Party Pack 8 to anyone looking for a good time with friends, or anyone who is just a fan of Jackbox in general. Then again you've probably already picked the game up if you're either of those.

My initial review of Jackbox 8 was absolutely glowing, I gave it a 9/10, and said it was the best one so far. 

I have no idea what I was on at the time, but I'm redoing this review as I think it completely missed the mark.

Jackbox 8 is fine, but it marks the end of the "golden age" of Jackbox, which I would define as 4-7. "Fine" is the key word I'd use to describe everything on show here, none of the games really stand out, but none of them are really terrible either. Weapons Drawn has a cool aesthetic, but it's the least interesting art game the team has ever produced. You get a letter, and you have to draw a weapon around that letter to make it hard to tell which letter you're hiding. It's a fine idea, but the restrictions make it almost impossible, the best way to win is to make fake red herring letters, and it just leads to everyone kind of bullshitting the game instead of actually playing it. Poll Mine is fun once or twice, but you need to have a big group of people that you know decently well, otherwise its a lot of shots in the dark, or there's not enough of you to make it interesting, and you can guess everything. Job Job is just rearranging letters to write something shocking, its the standard "play it once the first time you open the pack and never again" game. Drawful Animate is fun, but Drawful has always paled in comparison to Jackbox's cooler art games like Champ'd Up or TKO, and I find if your group doesn't have a lot of artists that people struggle a lot with the animation mechanic, simple as it is. Finally, The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is just another trivia game, but with some RNG to make sure the winner stays in the lead. Just a really weak collection of games, it's not one we ever really go back to, its just ok at best. 5/10.

I bought this game the day it came out, and wow. Wow wow wow. I had a LOT of fun playing it with my friends (Group of 6). I'll try and write a summary of each game and how much I enjoyed it.

Drawful Animate: Same ideas as past drawfuls, you just draw two frames this time. You can adjust the speed it flashes between the two, as well as having an onion skin available so you can see the previous frame.

Wheel of Enormous Proportions: What's a jackbox game without the trivia? Unlike past trivia games, there is more than one correct answer, and the more correct ones you click out of the dozen or so options, the more "slices" you get, that you then place on a wheel and spin for points.
Thoughts: I enjoyed it, but it wasn't everyone in my party's cup of tea. It is very RNG based, which led to someone who only got a handful of questions right end up winning anyways, while other people were getting more answers correct. Thoughts: Probably my favorite game out of the pack so far. My friends and I laughed our asses off the whole time over our dumb prompts. I also think it's cool how you can use any words on your screen and not just the sentences. Definitely one of the stronger ones out of the pack.

Poll Mine: Rate a group of objects, and guess what the most popular/least popular is (depending on the round)
Thoughts: I love the characters you get to choose from, and the game itself is also pretty entertaining. My friends and I enjoyed going against each other as teams and talking it out. All in all solid.

So let's have a little talk about the new jackbox party pack!

In this pack we have 4 brand new games and 1 returning one.
We have:
-Drawful: Animate (Return)
-The Wheel of Enormous Proportions
-Job Job
-The Poll Mine
-Weapons Drawn

Let's start with Drawful:
In drawful animate you get a secret prompt that you will have to draw/animate (a 2 frame animation). Once you have done that everyone will make a fake answer to make it look like that is the right answer to your animation while they will try to find the right answer hidden between all the other peoples fake answers.

-This is an alright game because its a returning game but it can still be fun. The prompts can be really weird or the most obvious thing ever but youll always have something to draw. Most of the time you'll look at your prompt and think how in gods name you will draw this but hey, thats the fun of it!


Next up Job Job:
In Job Job you will fill in ice breaker question and you can answer these how ever you like (this makes for the best words to use and that makes it even more fun). After these breakers have been answered you will get "classic" job interview question that you will have to answer with the words other people have used/made for you. Most funny answer, voted by the rest of the players, wins that round!

-This game is pretty relaxing and funny too. The amount of creativity you can put in your answers is all up to you and a little help by the other players. I really recommend you dont take the filling in of the ice breakers questions seriously because the weird sentences you get to make with the weirdest words is absolutely amazing.


Up nexto it's The Poll Mine:
In The Poll Mine you will get a category like: What is the best ice cream flavor?, Which tree would you be? or If you have to shop somewhere for the rest of your life where would you shop? (and thousands of others). When you get this category you will get a pre-set list of 8 answers and depending on the round you have to choose your 1st best answer, then 2nd, 3rd, etc. After everyone choose their answers they will compete in teams to try and find the best answers based on what everyone else also choose.

-This is a good and pretty competitive game i have to say. Most of the time you will be really surprised by what your fellow friends have put in as their favorite ice cream flavor. And the way some teams will scream at eachother is hilarious.


Aaaaand next is Weapons Drawn:
In Weapons Drawn you are detectives who will also try to commits some murders for extra points. At the start you will try to make two murder weapons that have one of the letters in your name hidden in it as your calling card. After you have drawn these weapons you will name an accomplice you brought with you to the party. After that is finally all set and done you will try to commit some murder by guessing which other player brought one of the accomplices. After that you will try to find out which person commited which murder but looking for clues in the weapons.

-Ive got to be completely honest with you, this game is not very great. The setup takes way longer then you might expect and the initial payoff isnt very not either. Ive played a round or two and i still dont quite understand what im doing. If this game wasnt as complicated and had less setup it might have been a little more fun but that wont really happen.


Last and never least its THE WHEEL OF ENORMOUS PROPORTIONS:
In The Wheel you first get to ask a burning question you always wanted answered and if you win the game you get this burning question answered too! After asking you will have to answer trivia questions to gain points and slices to put on the wheel for spinning. After 3 trivia questions have been asked you get to use the slices you have earned on the wheel to get even more points. This will keep happing until a player with 20.000 points lands with the winners wheel on a winning slice.

-This game is fun, not trivia murder party fun but still fun. Most of these trivia question arent actually that hard and most of the times if you just guess you will still get enough right to get enough points.


In summary this is another good pack with always some games that arent great but still a little fun.

Job Job - 8.5/10 - Always fun and always fair, never any dull answer.
The Poll Mine - 8.5/10 - Again surprisingly good, the competitive side makes it even more fun.
Weapons Drawn - 6/10 - Could be simpeler.
The Wheel of Enormous Proportions - 6.5/10 - Simpel but sometimes feels like its rigged (talking about you jasper).

Over all score: 7/10.

As far as the party packs go, pack 8 is solid. It certainly has its hits and misses, but overall I think it's a great addition to the series and worth buying if you like these sorts of party games! Below are my thoughts so far on the individual games:

~Drawful Animate~
-Hit or Miss: Hit!

If you don't like drawing games, this will be a miss, but surprisingly I think it's the best Drawful game so far. I've never been too into the other Drawful games compared to some of Jackbox's other drawing games (Tee-KO, Champ'd Up, Bidiots) and I figured this one would be a more tedious version of the other two because of the animation component. Surprisingly, the two-frame animation doesn't feel tedious and the ability to have two frames makes drawing the weird prompts feel more manageable and more fun! Plus, as more accurate drawings often lead to more accurate false responses, it's often more challenging to guess the prompt. Overall, while it isn't may favourite drawing game, I think it makes Drawful more fun and more worth throwing in during games night!

~Wheel of Enormous Proportions~
-Hit or Miss: Miss

I've never been huge a fan of most of Jackbox's trivia games (although I've had fun with Lie Swatter and Trivia Murder Party) but I don't really feel this game adds much to a trivia game formula except for more randomness to who wins. The questions are reasonable but the game has a lot of uncomfortable dialogue with the wheel and weird lottery system to choose a winner which to me feel random and unnecessary. The "asking a question to the wheel" gimmick is kinda neat, but feels like a tacked-on gimmick rather than an important part of the game. Overall it's a fine trivia game, but besides gimmicks that just add time between answering questions, I don't think it adds anything particularly meaningful that makes it more worth playing than Jackbox's better trivia games.

~The Poll Mine~
Hit or Miss: Hit?

This game can be quite a bit of fun with a good, larger group, but its point system is a bit odd and it's better in person than online. I think it's worth trying out to see whether or not it vibes well with your group, but it definitely feels most like a "worth playing every once in a few times" game rather than a big hit. That said, it's still good, but I'm not quite sure how to place it.

~Job Job~
Hit or Miss: Hit!!!

This is easily the best game in the pack in my opinion. It's easy to pick up, fun, quirky and not too serious. Of all the games here, it seems like the easiest to play multiple rounds of in succession like a Quiplash, Fibbage or Survive the Internet. Definitely worth a try!

~Weapons Drawn~
Hit or Miss: Hit

Of all games in this pack, this is the longest and most complicated. It has the potential to be a lot of fun, but you need people who are willing to take the effort to get into it. Because of its drawing components, it also may not be a hit with everyone. That said, it is a solid murder mystery game best played with people who know each other. There is lots of room for creativity with the weapons, difficult sleuthing with the weapons, and social, bluffing aspects. Importantly, each part of the game feels important to the overall experience. Overall, this game is fun and well-put together, but requires the right group to be enjoyed to its fullest.

Jackbox 8. My my my. There are quite a lot of good games to be found here, but I do still think that it's probably a step down from the last pack (although to be fair, pack 7 was damn near perfect, and whatever followed it was unlikely to be able to compare to it). Compared to all the packs, I would rank them as follows: 1<2<3<6<5<8<4<7.

Looking at the individual games, we have Job Job, the funny game in the pack, Weapons Drawn, the unique drawing game in the pack which was mixed with some social deduction, Wheel of Enormous Proportions, the trivia game of the pack, Drawful 2, the remake game of the pack mixed with drawing, and Poll Mine, the unique game of the pack. I will give each of these games their own individual mini-reviews, as well as score them out of 10 rather than 5, because I'm feeling a bit like Fantano.

Drawful Animate: This game is kind of a dud if I'm being honest, which is weird because it shouldn't be; it's a remake. Drawful Animate is basically Drawful, but you are allowed to draw one extra frame, to make your pictures "animated" (you probably could've guessed that lmao). This game blows, because there are already better versions of this game that exist. If you like the long slow and tedious task of animating drawings, play Gartic Phone. It's free and it's online, so you can play that with your friends. And if you enjoy the fast-paced gameplay of Drawful, just buy Drawful 2. It's relatively cheap, and maybe a few of you guys might already own it, as it was given out for free last year. This game is outclassed by other existing games, and because of that, it's not a super memorable game to play, compared to those other party games. For that, I would give it a 3/10.

Wheel of Enormous Proportions: The trivia game of the pack. This game works pretty well as a trivia game, as the questions perfectly balance on the line of being not well known enough to be easy, but not obscure enough to be hard. However, the trivia is not the point of the game. The trivia serves as a way to score points on the wheel. The wheel is admittedly kind of divisive. I personally enjoy rng-based gameplay, so it's something that I personally enjoy, however, if you are a person who wants to win after getting the most points out of everyone, do note that this is not guaranteed, and you're probably better off playing You Don't Know Jack or Trivia Murder Party 1 or 2 off of the other packs. Overall, from my personal party, we would probably rate it a 8/10, but if you personally don't like rng, it's probably not going to be any higher than a 5/10 for you.

Job Job: This game is proof that broken english is funny. Basically, all you do is answer weird interview questions, then use other people's responses to answer other questions. It's basically quiplash but the words are not your own. Now I know that me describing it makes it sound very frustrating, but you're gonna have to trust me on this. This game is objectively one of the most fun games off of the pack. 9.5/10

Poll Mine: This game is basically Family Feud. It's a fun game, but if I'm being totally honest, my friends and I didn't get much out of this game. I think that maybe if it's played with a large audience and a lot of people, then you might be able to get the feeling that people were actually interviewed, and were polled. But with only 5 people, it's pretty easy to just gang up as a team, and tell everyone to pick the same option for number one, which can lead to it being shockingly easy to guess which is what. I think this game could be an 8/10 with an audience, but as it is with only 5 people, it's a 4/10 for me.

Weapons Drawn: Man, people really don't like this game huh. I understand where their criticism is coming from, as there are quite a lot of unnecessary elements in this game, that are pretty much detrimental to understanding the game. That being said, my party of 5 actually did understand what was going on here, and because of that, we were able to have a lot of fun with this. The accomplice system can lead to some funnies, because you can name you accomplice whatever you want them to be, meaning that you can name your accomplice John F. Kennedy, then someone will assassinate him. But I think the biggest flaw is that the letters that are meant to serve as clues can very easily be scribbled over, making it shockingly impossible to guess who the murderer is. This game is very fun, if you know what you're doing, but explaining it to people who don't is probably going to be a challenge (which is why I abstained from doing so lmao). As it is though, I think this game is a 7/10.

Overall, averaging out the scores, this pack would be a 6.5/10 from my party, or a 5.9/10 if you're a third party. It's worth the buy, but do note that there are a few experimental games here that you may or may not like.

I own all the other packs and I think I can comfortably say that this is either the 2nd or 3rd best one (best obviously being 3, second place maybe going to 7).

Disclaimer: Haven't gotten around to playing Weapons Drawn just yet, if I remember that I wrote this later on I'll update it for that game. Anyways, about the other 4...
Also I like making tier lists so I'll give each game an approximate tier list ranking.

Drawful Animate:
I think this one doesn't get quite enough credit. While it seems like the only main new gimmick of this game compared to its previous versions is the whole "animation" thing (which still allows for some funnier artwork imo), it has a second much more subtle change as well. The prompts.
Normally in the "lie detection" games (Drawfuls and Fibbages) it's very easy to identify certain wrong answers due to spelling, grammar, or punctuation use. Drawful Animate throws that all out the window with some of the weirdest prompts I've ever seen. The game even gave me a prompt that was deliberately spelled wrong! This means the game is a lot more "how well do you know your friends' brains" and a lot less "did you do well in high school english class."
However if you already own an older drawful and didn't notice/care for this trend while playing, you may be better off sticking to it instead.
RANK: Low A tier

Wheel of Enormous Proportions:
While it's certainly not as good as the Trivia Murder Party games, this one is still alright. The format of the questions switches up often enough to keep things from getting too stale. The wheel spinning does seem to be a bit more of the focus though, which may not be your cup of tea if you prefer competitive trivia. The delay between questions is also longer than in TMP, but is still quicker than YDKJ.
If you want hardcore trivia, this probably isn't for you. But if you enjoy getting screwed over sometimes and screaming at your friends at the top of your lungs, then this game is a good choice. 
RANK: Mid B tier

Job Job:
Holy crap this game is just so good. I would say it's better than all 3 Quiplashes and maybe even good enough to take the crown from Surviving the Internet as the best Jackbox game overall. 
The game is similar to Quiplash in that you're coming up with comedic responses to prompts and pairing off against each other, but the main difference is that your friends get to do the heavy lifting by providing you with lots of words to pick from based on a personal response prompt (like in STI). This results in absolutely hilarious answers that look like they were written by a serial killer. The game also has a few easter eggs and lots of references for those who like that kind of thing.
The verdict's in folks. Job Job is an absolutely incredible game that represents a new gold standard for the Jackbox series.
RANK: S+

Poll Mine: Currently my least favourite game (haven't played Weapons Drawn yet though). It isn't bad though, just not nearly as good as the others. The concept of a team based escape game is fun and creative (I think this is actually the first Team vs Team Jackbox game, which is surprising), but it has a couple things holding it back. 
1. The 3 rounds (as far as I can tell) are always the same. You'll always be trying to find the exact same positions in the poll each game you play. This is the same reason I slightly prefer Quiplash 2 over the other 2 games; the final round is not the same style each time. 
2. You have to rank too many things in the later rounds. I think that 3 is excellent number to stay at for the whole game. 4 is alright sometimes, but by 5 I find that people approach "impartial" territory with the rankings.
Despite its flaws though, this game is still pretty fun, and the teams thing gives it some uniqueness.
RANK: Low B

Overall, pack 8 is a solid entry in the series. It's possibly worth getting for Job Job alone, but the other games do pull their weight as well. (I doubt my thoughts on WD will change this point much lol)

I own all the packs, played every game several times, yada yada.
The TL;DR is that this is another great entry but it might not be worth the retail of $30.
[i]Here's the individual reviews:[/i]

[b][u]Drawful Animate:[/u][/b]
Translating animation into an accessible party game is an interesting approach for sure; Unfortunately it's executed sloppily. Drawful Animate has difficulty justifying the animation angle that's been introduced. The obvious strength of animation is conveying actions or sequences that would otherwise be difficult using a single frame; The problem is many of the prompts in Animate don't contain verbs/actions that would make good use of the 2nd frame, and instead are mostly prompts you could easily do with a single picture. It results in a lesser Drawful that takes twice as long. [b]2.5/5[/b]

[b][u]The Wheel of Enormous Proportions:[/u][/b]
It would appear this is already the most controversial entry in Party Pack 8; Not just online, but even among the multiple friend groups I've tried the game with. This is a trivia game with a very heavy RNG slant. I had one group that thoroughly enjoyed it, and another that were actively agitated since most of the game is focused on the wheel opposed to the trivia itself. I personally enjoy it and it's arguably the most well-paced game on here, but if you don't like luck based games or trivia, this likely won't click with you. [b]3/5[/b]

[b][u]Job Job:[/u][/b]
A Quiplash-esque game that works way better than you may expect. You type in a response to a question asked on your device; Then other players need to rearrange the words in your response to answer a completely different question. The limitations of what you have to work with result in broken, scattered-minded answers that end-up feeling a lot less [i]'witty'[/i] than Quiplash, but it's also why the game works so well. [b]4.5/5[/b]

[b][u]The Poll Mine:[/u][/b]
This plays a lot like [i]"Family Feud"[/i] where the players are split into 2 teams, and need to guess the top answers out of everything presented. Trying to talk to your partners about what everyone voted for without giving away too much to the other team makes for a deceptively strategic experience. It's a very socially driven game and always leads to good discussions. The element of [i]"torches"[/i] that basically act as lives is a great idea and the entire progression of the game feels fully realized. Feels like you could probably speed this one up and slip in another round, but otherwise, Poll Mine might be the best in Pack 8. [b]4.5/5[/b]

[b][u]Weapons Drawn:[/u][/b]
This is easily the most complicated drawing game [i](Bidiots being a surprisingly far second[/i]) and might even be one of the most complicated Party Pack games ever; I'd argue even more so than Push The Button despite that game involving much more strategy. Players play the role as both detectives, and murderers. You draw murder weapons, choose an accomplice to murder, and figure out who drew what weapons. Between trying to hide calling cards in your own art, and discussing with other players who did what, there's a lot going on here; It'll take a game or two before you get a full grasp on it. Props to Weapons Drawn for being the most conceptually creative game here, but transitions between rounds go on for far too long and overall it's a fairly slow game. Between all of the Jack Box social deduction games [i](Faking It, Push the Button,)[/i] this is the weakest we've seen. [b]2.5/5[/b]


This is the first Jackbox with 2 drawing games which makes this a less varied pack than 7; And considering those 2 games are some of the weaker drawing entries we've seen [i](especially compared to last year's Champ'd Up,)[/i] it's hard to justify that decision. Regardless; Party Pack 8 takes a lot of risks, and a lot of those risks definitely pay off. I can easily see myself coming back to this one a lot for Job Job and Poll Mine alone; But if you're not a huge Jackbox buff and want to know which game to start with, packs 3 and 7 will provide much more bang for your buck.

I own all of the Jackbox Party Packs up to date, and I can definitely say this pack has already climbed its way up my ranks. If you want my short, sweet recommendation for this party pack overall, it'll be at the very bottom of my review. Games-wise, I will explain Weapons Drawn last because it's got quite a bit of significance to me and it's a lot to take in.

I'll try to keep the other games simple:

[b] Drawful Animate [/b]
Drawful except you draw a second frame to make an animation. I've seen some people mention the extended amount of time, or that some prompts are difficult to execute via drawing two panels. Yes, I will admit, some of the new prompts are very "What the hell?," but it adds to the funny factor as you grapple with how to draw it. Longer wait times was never an issue for my friend group. Drawful Animate is a great game that offered a lot of amusement.

[b] The Wheel of Enormous Proportions [/b]
Jackbox definitely took a step in a different direction with this game, (in a good way). It's a trivia game that could be compared to the difficulty of the Trivia Murder Parties where almost no one knows many of the answers, but you're able to select numerous answers so you have a better fighting chance. Depending on how well you do in the rounds, you obtain "slices" to put into the wheel to earn jackpots to get you that sweet victory. Here's the catch though, the RNG for the wheel is horrendous. I personally did not mind it, as it spiced up the game and kept it going as everyone was neck-and-neck by that point in the match. This may turn some people away from the game, however, because you may be in first for a good chunk of the game and get the title ripped away from you at the very end. If you dislike poor RNG and/or somewhat random winners, I'd suggest you stray away from this game.

[b] Job Job [/b]
I'd say this game was the most humorous out of all that are offered in this pack. You basically make anagrams out of a pool of words from the other player's responses at the beginning of the game. Fortunately for me, my friends had very.. Interesting responses to say the least and it provided good content for our answers, lmao. Definitely give this game a shot when you try the pack.

[b] The Poll Mine [/b]
I heard someone say this is like "Family Feud," and they are definitely right. Each round has a different twist, however. For example: You cannot pick the #1 answer, or you must answer which is the lowest score and move your way on up to the #1 answer. It's a clever and sneaky little game trying to deduce what the answers may be without letting the enemy team get too much insight on what your team picked for their answers. I also highly recommend this game, but I can see some people being turned away from it because of debate purposes. It's worth giving a shot, though!

Lastly,

[h1] Weapons Drawn [/h1]
Jackbox took a giant leap with this game, and honestly, I loved it. It's a very fleshed out game, and to be honest, it is probably the MOST complex game that Jackbox has ever created. Although I loved the game, I must also admit that it is very difficult to understand, and you will have to play it several times to get a decent grasp on how things run in it. In all honesty, I think part of the confusion drawn from this game comes from the players, too. This game gets quite complicated because you as the player are both a detective, and a murderer. Everyone brings a guest of their own to the party, and you must name your guest that you have brought. Once all the guests are presented, everyone must start guessing which player they think brought who (the guests). If you guess correctly, you murder the guest and get a murder point. That seems simple enough, until you have to start finding out who was behind the murders. Everyone had to draw murder weapons at the beginning of the game, disguising a letter the game assigned to them based off of the nickname they joined the game with. In order to throw people off, you are suggested to try and incorporate other letters so that yours isn't obvious. [b] This is why I'm led to believe that part of the confusion comes from the players themselves. [/b] The game becomes very complex because of the clever ways everyone tries to incorporate their letter into their weapon, and working around it to seem like it was someone else. It isn't all the players' fault for the complexity, however. Jackbox, after all, allowed for this to take place, and they even suggest it. Although yes, I thoroughly enjoyed Weapons Drawn, I cannot deny that I was scratching my head most of the duration of the game.
Game mechanics and gameplay itself aside, the art, music, and ambience were phenomenal.
Would I recommend Weapons Drawn? Absolutely, yes. However, keep in mind that this game requires a lot more thinking  and deduction than all of Jackbox's other games, (with the exception of Push the Buttton).

Weapons Drawn Tl;dr:
Frustrating to figure out and complicated as hell, but definitely fun and worth it as it pushes you to think creatively and cleverly. Great job on this one, Jackbox. You've outdone yourselves.

[h1] Jackbox took some BOLD leaps on this pack, and it was definitely worth it. I highly recommend this game!! [/h1]
This is easily the strongest Jackbox Pack yet.

Overall: Probably the best pack since 3, all of the games in it are solid and there's a really good range of game types.  I would highly recommend this one if you are just looking to purchase a single pack.

Weapons Drawn: A really clever combination of Social Deduction and Art games, where you have to hide a provided letter in multiple drawings and try and figure out the letters of other players to catch them in murders.  Definitely the most complicated of the pack, but fun once you learn it.  This one could use some balancing, though:  I had a game with the letter N, which is really diverse in all of the forms the game lets you use (lowercase vs. uppercase, cursive vs. normal).  I was carried really hard by my letter and no one guessed me for any murder.  Maybe if we could use shapes instead (or a smaller letter pool), that may balance the game more effectively.

Poll Mine: Probably better for streamers who can get a huge range of answers from their chat, but still really fun with a small group!  You get into teams and try to determine the top answers for a given question.  The team aspect is really interesting since you have to be careful what all you tell your team, at the risk of the other team getting valuable clues for their turn.

Drawful Animate: Basically Drawful 3, and Drawful was already one of the top Jackbox games.  The animation part doesn't completely change the game; it just adds new options to the original gameplay, which is nice.  The game's prompts really surprised us, since they're much more natural (ex. mispellings, bad grammar, abbreviations).  I kinda wish there was an option to turn mispellings off, but it's not a bad thing and makes the game a lot more interesting in some cases (and gives people a chance if they accidentally misspell something). 

The Wheel of Enormous Proportions:  A really chill trivia game, and a great way to start a Jackbox session with friends.  The questions can be pretty tough and interesting, and the wheel provides a good amount of luck for those who can't seem to get the questions right (aka me).  This one probably has the best art and vibes, a really good calm game to play.

Job Job:  The standout title of this pack, it's a blast.  You have to answer random questions, then take the words from everyone's responses and use them to answer job interview questions.  The potential for people's answers is huge, and my friend group was laughing like crazy at the sentences we could create.  It's a pretty simple idea, but it goes a long way without any extra gimmicks needed.

I like to do first impression reviews of new Jackbox packs, so here goes.

Drawful Animate: Based on one game, I'd say it's the weakest in the pack. The animation factor doesn't really add that much, so it's still a very basic drawing guessing game. The prompts are also very obscure and can lead to multiple people guessing very similar things. Pretty mediocre game, especially compared to Champ'd Up from the last pack which knocked it out of the park.

The Wheel of Enormous Proportions: I love a good trivia game (Trivia Murder Party 2 is my all-time favourite Jackbox game), but sadly this isn't it. The trivia itself is solid and includes some different formats of question which is cool, and the overall presentation is really enjoyable. Unfortunately, the game itself ends up being more about luck than general knowledge, so you can feel cheated by the RNG gods.

Job Job: Now we're getting into the good stuff. This is definitely one of the best Jackbox games yet and arguably the one that generates the most laughs. It's hard to fault it, really!

The Poll Mine: Right up there with Job Job in my opinion. The teamwork aspect is great and probably works better than in any previous team-based Jackbox game. I also like that it's based on the opinions of your fellow players rather than random surveys which allows you to gauge your choices based on your knowledge of your friends (and sometimes makes you despair at their choices).

Weapons Drawn: I think of all the games in this pack, this is the one I like the most conceptually. The idea of trying to conceal a letter within your art is great, then the deception and deduction added on top is fantastic. In my opinion, though, the game itself doesn't quite live up to the expectations the concept creates. Once you know who has what letter, it's too easy to figure out who each killer is, especially if the artist has a distinctive style. On top of that, the cold cases can make the game drag towards the end.

Overall, I'd say 8 is a step down from 7, which itself was a step down from 6 (the best pack in my opinion). The only games I can see becoming staples for my group are Job Job and Poll Mine. Drawful Animate especially seems like a game someone would want to play once, then abandon it in favour of better drawing games like Champ'd Up and Tee K.O.
Still recommended, though!

This pack is worth it just for Job Job. It's my favorite Jackbox game of all time. However, here's a review of all the games:

Dawful Animate - This is just drawful, but slightly more complicated. You can draw two panels instead of one and it switches back and forth between them. It's probably best you only play it with people who have played the original drawful. In my opinion, simpler is better here. Just play Drawful.

I was excited to play The Wheel of Enormous Proportions. Unfortunately, it feels much more luck based than it should be for a trivia game. Pretty much all the points awarded at the end seem to just come from spinning the wheel, and actually getting the trivia right is just fluff in the middle.

Job Job is the best. You write answers to prompts, but that's really just giving people words for the next part. You have to answer questions using the word salad you get from the mixture of other people's answers. It always makes people laugh.

I enjoy poll mine. First, it asks you a question and you're supposed to rank the answers given to you from 1st to last. Then, you and your team (everyone is split into two teams), all collaborate together to determine things like "What's the most popular answer?" In later rounds, you'll have to pick things like "What's the least popular answer?" It's actually pretty interesting.

Weapons Drawn is not fun. It feels like there's way too much going on and even by the end of the game, everyone doesn't fully understand what's happening. Essentially, you're supposed to kill people and then draw a murder weapon based on a prompt, but you have to hide a letter that's in your name somewhere in the drawing. That premise by itself is only okay at best, so they tried to add a bunch of other guessing stuff in there that's just a little too confusing and the whole thing falls really flat. If I were to rank all the Jackbox games from every pack so far, this one might be dead last.

Party Pack 8 is similar to other packs in that there are one to two games worth playing along with some real duds.  

Job Job: Job Job was probably the game my group enjoyed most, players answer "interview" questions with the individual words that other plays answer unrelated prompts with, so it could be difficult if the person who provided you with the prompts really phoned it in.  Has a very Quiplash/Survive the Internet slant.

Poll Mine: This is a "family feud" type game, where the group votes on questions and are split into two teams to guess how each answer was ranked.  A nice slant, was you aren't always after the most popular answer, but sometimes the second or fifth.  

Weapons Drawn: Is a fun social deception game, but is much much too long.  There is a "hurry" button like in Push the Button, but even with everyone spamming that, the game is a bit of slog.  Cool premise though.

Wheel of Enormous Proportions: This might be the worst game in the whole Jackbox catalog.  The game is about 90% RNG from the wheel and 10% trivia. Our group did not have fun with this one at all.

Drawful Animate:  I was looking forward to this one the most, because our group loves the drawing games, but it left us a little disappointed.  The actual drawing tools are VERY simple, only a few colors to work with, no options to change the brush thickness, no eraser/undo button, and the prompts can be VERY abstract making conveying your prompt difficult with the limited tools.  A GREAT feature I'm shocked that isn't in the game is the ability to "copy" your first drawing to the second frame for animation purposes.  At present, the game shows you an outline only and you have to re-draw it a second time.

It's worth getting, but I would recommend a sale. I like playing it because it has wheel of enormous proportions, which is like trivia murder party but more pop culture in my opinion. Job job is also fun even if it devolves into vulgarity. The others I haven't really touched but they're fun as well when you understand them. All in all 7/10

My friends and I love all the Jackbox games, this one being no exception, but this one does have some problems worth mentioning that stuck out to us right away that I feel like should be mentioned.

Pole Mine is a fun game in concept but without a lot of players and/or an audience the end results end up skewed and sometimes feel entirely wrong. 

Weapons Drawn is your fun murder mystery of the pack, with one key flaw that can make the game very difficult to play. This one can be entirely derailed if your players only draw letters and scribbles to hide the letter. By doing this it can be very difficult to play.

Job Job is just plain fun, end of story. If you loved games Blather Around and Quiplash, this game is the prodigy child of the two and I couldn't love a game more. My only problem with it is that you are able to click on your name to add it to the answer, but it doesn't let you choose an individual word from your name, instead the entire name gets put in. 

I went into Drawful Animate expecting it to be the worst one, no questions asked. It is only another remade game with barely any change right? Wrong, so very wrong. By simply adding a second frame to give your drawing life, it changes the entire game, making it an incredibly fun game to play. They even added shortened words and slang to make it harder to guess which one was written by the game. My only complaint with this one is that you can't put down the same answer as another player. If you do it gives you a prompt telling you it is too close to either the answer or what another person wrote. One of my favorite things in these kinds of games are the end of round screen coming up and seeing two people wrote the same obscure lie, so it is really sad that it is no longer a thing.

Last and most certainly least is The Wheel of Enormous Proportions. Jackbox has always been king when it came down to trivia games. For example, the Trivia Murder Parties. With TMP, you got both real and the occasional goofy trivia question with a fun penalty game to do if you got it wrong, all with the theme of a murder hotel. Wheel of Enormous Proportions is not that, not clever, not too funny, not well themed, not fun. You are given select all that apply questions that give you the ability to put your name on the wheel. As of now I have no plans of returning to the Wheel, but to my knowledge there isn't any mini-games or special quirks either. After putting your name on the Wheel at certain tiles you have people spin arbitrarily for random amounts of points, then rinse and repeat until someone wins with a certain amount. When you win, you get your question put against the Jackbox team's version of a larger word count magic 8 ball. Without a doubt in my mind this game is the least fun of the pack and its lack of fun gimmicks or any good mechanics make it easier to decide what to play when the list of games is whittled down by one.

While these complaints exist, they are currently the only real complaints I have. This pack is nowhere near being the best pack but is far from the worst. Worth the money spent and I will be playing again (except for Wheel of Enormous Proportions, all my homies hate Wheel of Enormous Proportions).

While I personally love all the games in this pack, they're all an acquired taste more than an instant love.

Drawful Animate is a fun time that everyone I've played with enjoys, but it's purposefully clunky drawing portion means that you end up playing this one entirely for the absurdity of it, rather than to try and make detailed abominations. 

The Wheel of Enormous Proportions is a toss-up between players: either you think it's one of the best trivia games so for, or you hate the RNG of it with a passion. It's bullsh*t, but the bullsh*t is where most of the fun is. This game is what I'd call the "dust collector" of the pack just because of how divided opinions on it are.

Job Job tends to be most peoples favorite, but it requires everyone to be funny in order for it to work. It also has the Talking Points issue of where it fundamentally doesn't work as a competitive game, but is incredibly fun to play casually. Whether or not you enjoy this one depends on the group you're playing with.

Poll Mine is an interesting idea with various ways of playing it (the best IMO being everyone in a room, but not physically split into teams). Great for a competitive/cooperative showdown, but could easily wear out unless you really enjoy the game play of it.

Weapons Drawn is probably my favorite Jackbox game of all time, but it's also the black sheep of the pack (and arguably, of all the packs). It's the most complicated jackbox game by far, and requires a good knowledge on what to do in order to fully be able to enjoy it. It feels less like a "jackbox game", and more like a full social deduction/strategy game. The issue there is that if your just casually going through the pack, a high-strategy and deduction game isn't really gonn be what you're looking for. Weapons Drawn is a game that takes time to learn, time that other jackbox games don't ask of you. 

Overall: not as good of a pack as 7 (which was basically the perfect pack), and definitely not the best starter pack (that would be #3), but still one worthy of being picked up if any of the games seem appealing to you. You'll either love 'em or hate 'em.

The Jackbox Party Pack 8 might as well be my second-favorite Party Pack in the series. It really boils down to how each game has been an enjoyable experience, even if one of them is literally Mario Party Trivia but I'll get to him soon.

First, may I present the best Jackbox game of all time: [b]Job Job[/b]. "WHAAAAT?! Even better than Quiplash?" Yes, hear me out. While Quiplash has been the series that introduced me to Jackbox and I have held the series of games in my heart, a lot of things that Job Job does compared to Quiplash hits harder. First, the way you input response isn't just typing words to use against others. You are instead using words that were written by other players during the first part the icebreakers. While this can be a make or break for some, it's way easier to create a response to the interview question than say Quiplash. Quiplash is awesome, yes, but there are prompts that are difficult to shallow and find a funny response that the other players will like. With Job Job, broken words pulled from the players (and from the question itself too, even your own name!) can make the funniest responses no matter how poorly written it is. Tho the game does drag long given the circumstances of getting your response, it doesn't really matter. Plus waiting is so enjoyable thanks to M. Bubbles being the best water-cooler out there doing some funny stuff that only they can do. And the motivation posters, the art style of Owen Watson, the amazing soundtrack, 10 players, and the WordArt! And by far one of the best credit songs ever written. While I do like to play Quiplash every once in a while, Job Job is a phenomenal game. I honestly really hope that we can eventually enter our own questions (UGC) similar to Quiplash and Drawful, but maybe for a sequel? Or if Jackbox updates their own games. Either one can come. Anyways M. Bubz rules!

[b]Drawful: Animate[/b] is yet another outstanding entry in the Drawful series. Unlike the other two entries, this time you're drawing two frames of animation. Onion skinning is available to help out make your animation a reality. The prompts in Drawful: Animate especially have nailed how people typically write their titles. Typos, weird punctuation, it really feels like they nailed their game here, and it blends so nicely with everyone else's prompt. My only problem is again time, but with the new capacity of 10 players, some quality of life changes (like the game auto-submitting your animation even if you don't finish on time), and the host being cheeky as always, this is a fun Drawful experience, and I can't recommend enough.

[b]The Poll Mine[/b] is an interesting concept. Split into two teams, you are asked a survey question and have to rank the options (three in round 1, four in round 2, five in round 3). Afterwards, the fun can begin. In round 1, you have to find the top three answers. In round 2, you have to find the fourth, third, and second most selected answers and try not to select the most-selected one. And then round 3 is to find the options from bottom to top. Now, there are some things to consider in this game. Firstly, it is within your best interests not to reveal too much of what you answered, because the other team can take advantage of what you said to try to get the correct answer. Secondly, this game isn't fun with less players. Having only four people split evenly with two player cannot give enough answer survey responses to fill in. It'll make the final round harder to do. Finally, this game is actually pretty chill. Regardless of my issue with player counts, this game has a relaxing mood, from visuals to soundtrack. And I cannot commend the artists who went out of their way to make a unique artstyle for this game. Now while I think some of the survey questions can be questionable at best, it does allow us to have a meaningful discussion on what people voted for and why. So while I have some problems, this game is cool at best.

[b]Weapons Drawn[/b] has a very interesting and amazing concept. Every player is a detective, but also a murderer, and it's your goal to solve and commit crims. But everyone cannot just kill without a weapon, drawn by the player. These weapons require that the player hides a calling card, a letter from their name. If you are playing this, I recommend you try to rename yourself to something that cannot easily be traced right back to you. Letters like P, R, or J can be extremely difficult to hide. Moreso, having a letter like Y in your name can make it easy for a murderer to kill your accomplice, which you name in secret after your two weapons are drawn. Once some murders are committed, the investigation (and social deduction) can begin. Important notes, the murderer cannot be the person who brought the victim, nor any other individuals whose first weapon they have dropped shares similar weapons to the object that killed the accomplice. If you are successful at finding the murder, you get points, but select wrongly, and you get nothing. After another round with you drawing two more weapons and another accomplice, the final round, Cold Cases, is a lightning round of all the unsolved cases. As the detective, it is in your best interests to find the murderer on time, but as the murderer, it is also in your best interest to deflect everyone to earn points. Once everything is tallied up, the winner is declared. If all of this sounded too complicated to you, that's because it is. There is a lot to unpack with Weapons Drawn, but I don't think it's a bad experience. It's fun when you get to murder people, but there have been cases when one player will leave the game without having the opportunity to kill anyone, which happened to me once. Not only that, but it can be easy to cheese just by drawing some mumbo jumbo. Despite these issues, this game is really enjoyable to play. Mostly I give it props for the amazing soundtrack by Elise Wattman, who started her career with this game. The investigation discussion is fun, the accomplices names can be funny at times, and while I feel some stuff can be done better, this was a solid game.

This leaves [b]The Wheel of Enormous Proportions[/b] in last place for this Pack, but I also don't think this one bad. This is moreso a trivia game mixed with Mario Party. You can only win once you hit 20,000 points and spin your name on the Winner Wheel, but you'll have more chances by answering trivia questions right, most being multiple-choice.
